name: Co-operative compliance desk: accounts, audit and AGM pack for small koperasi
buyer: Small and dormant-risk koperasi (committee volunteers or part-time secretaries); about 9,800 active of 16,009 registered
trigger: Co-operative Societies Act 1993 s58 (accounts within 30 days of each transaction, books ready within 2 months of year end) and s61 approved auditor (SKM GP26 of 1 Sep 2024); audited accounts to SKM at least 30 days before AGM, AGM by 30 June; Feb 2026 ministry warning of funding freeze or legal action for poor performers (federal, SKM).
evidence: https://thesun.my/news/malaysia-news/over-7000-cooperatives-fail-to-maintain-accounts-skm-offers-guidance-support-ramanan-gg13401135/ (fetched: 7,779 failed to maintain accounts, 2,304 not audited, grant RM3,000/RM3,500); https://skm.gov.my/images/01-utama/perundangan/garis-panduan/gp26-01-09-2024.pdf ; https://www.malaymail.com/amp/news/malaysia/2026/02/11/funding-only-for-performing-cooperatives-poor-performers-face-freeze-or-legal-action-ministry-warns/208860 ; https://www.skm.gov.my/images/01-utama/perundangan/pekeliling-skm/SURAT-PEKELILING-PENGAWALSELIAAN-AKTIVITI-KREDIT-KOPERASI.pdf
existing: Free p-SKM Excel accounting tool (2014-15, support status unknown); SPBK from MOCCIS (commercial, older brochure, loan/member modules). No cloud product found in the search.
unchecked: Current SKM reporting format and portal (e-Koperasi not confirmed); exact late-filing penalties; willingness to pay by volunteer committees; whether grants can fund software; SKM circular on credit-activity regulation just surfaced and not read.

first_check.duty: Section 61 of the Co-operative Societies Act 1993 (Act 502), restated in SKM guideline GP26 of 1 Sep 2024: accounts must be audited at least once each financial year by an SKM-approved auditor. Koperasi that run no business, hold no AGM and have no audit for more than 3 years face cancellation (SKM Negeri Sembilan director, BH Apr 2026). Offences under the Act can be compounded under the Cooperatives (Compounding of Offences) Regulations 2010 (s93). I could not reach or verify the s58 text, the 30-day pre-AGM submission rule, the 30 June AGM date or the penalty amounts: the Act PDF and GP26 PDF did not render (503), and Malaymail returned 403.
first_check.market: About 16,000 registered koperasi, per the claim; the Nov 2019 figure was about 14,000, of which about 4,200 were dormant. The Dec 2024 Bernama/The Sun report gives 7,779 koperasi failing to keep accounts and 2,304 unaudited. Negeri Sembilan alone has 768 registered koperasi, 340 of them inactive (Apr 2026). I did not re-confirm the claim's 9,800 active / 16,009 registered from an SKM statistic.
first_check.competitor: MOCCIS SPBK: web-based, bilingual, koperasi-specific accounting and member-loan system that says it complies with SKM financial-statement reporting guidelines and was evaluated by SKM. Its flyer is old and I found no price. p-SKM: free SKM Excel accounting tool from 2014-15; I don't know if it is still maintained. ANGKASA: its recovery division helps dormant koperasi prepare account statements, and with SKM and IKMa it gives free POS and website help. SKM: grant of RM3,000 (Peninsular) or RM3,500 (Sabah/Sarawak) for audit and accounting, plus guidance and training. I found no koperasi compliance or AGM-pack cloud SaaS in Malaysia. memberAMS is generic membership software.
first_check.reason: The duty is real. SKM guideline GP26 (Sept 2024) requires each koperasi to have an SKM-approved auditor audit its accounts every year under s61 of Act 502. Dormant koperasi that skip audits and AGMs for more than 3 years risk cancellation (SKM N9, Apr 2026). I could not read the s58 text, the submission deadline or the penalty amounts. Pain is wide: 7,779 koperasi do not keep accounts and 2,304 are unaudited. But others already cover part of the job. MOCCIS SPBK is web accounting built to SKM reporting rules, and p-SKM is a free Excel tool. ANGKASA's recovery division prepares accounts, and SKM grants RM3,000 to RM3,500. The audit itself needs a human approved auditor. Dormant koperasi have no income, so few will pay. I can't confirm that nothing does the core job.

challenge_check.killer: None found. Partial overlaps: MOCCIS SPBK (koperasi accounting and member system, which says it was evaluated by SKM; current status and price unknown), free SKM p-SKM Excel tool (2014), the SKM accounting and audit grant of RM3,000/RM3,500 that pays accountants, and ANGKASA's annual-accounts recovery service (Khidmat Pemulihan Perakaunan Tahunan; details unverified).
challenge_check.reason: I found nothing that does the full job. Searches in Malay and English turned up no cloud tool that takes a koperasi from SKM-format accounts through audit prep to the AGM pack. The only koperasi-specific tools are MOCCIS SPBK (web-based, launched 2004, 2016 flyer, no price) and SKM's free Excel tool p-SKM (2014). The duty still bites: Act 502 s60/61 requires an annual audit by an SKM-approved auditor. I found no small-koperasi exemption. Koperasi that stay inactive for over 3 years face cancellation (Negeri Sembilan, Apr 2026), and Sarawak cancelled 61 in 2023-25. The market is weak, though. Most of the 7,779 non-compliant bodies are dormant, run by volunteers and short of cash. The RM3,000/RM3,500 SKM grant goes to accountants and auditors, and approved audit firms already do bookkeeping bundled with the audit. I couldn't confirm SKM's submission portal or late-filing penalties.
